parsed.summary: The Lean target claims some finitely presented group is not sofic. But `Sofic` is defined with the contradictory hypothesis `0 < ε → ε < 0 → ε < 1`, so every group is vacuously sofic and the target is false as stated. Also, the paper's Theorem 1.1 is about the Leavitt unit group, not finite presentability, so the target does not match the excerpt.

glossary.plain: Normalized Hamming distance between two permutations of a finite set Y: (#points where they differ)/|Y|.
A map from G to Sym(n) with n>0 sending 1 to identity (not necessarily a homomorphism).
glossary.standard_concept: map to a finite symmetric group used in soficity

glossary.plain: On a finite set F, the map is ε-multiplicative and every non-identity element of F moves more than a 1-ε fraction of points.
For all finite F and ε, if 0<ε, ε<0 and ε<1 then a good model exists. The hypotheses are contradictory, so this holds for every group.
glossary.note: Intended: 0<ε → ε<1 → ∃ M, GoodOn M F ε. The extra ε<0 makes the property vacuous.

lean_claims.plain: There exists a group G (in Type) that is finitely presented and for which the vacuous Sofic class fails. Since every group satisfies the vacuous Sofic, this is false.

paper_claims.plain: The unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra L_{F2}(1,2) is not sofic.

coverage.why: The Lean statement is an existence claim for a finitely presented non-sofic group, not the Leavitt unit group. Finite presentability is not in the excerpt. The Sofic definition is also vacuous.

flags.explanation: The hypotheses `0 < ε → ε < 0 → ε < 1` are mutually contradictory, so Sofic holds for every group. ¬Sofic G is then false for all G, so the target theorem is unprovable (false) as stated.
flags.probe_idea: example (G : Type) [Group G] : SoficGroups.Sofic G := ⟨fun F ε h1 h2 _ => absurd (h1.trans h2) (lt_irrefl _)⟩

flags.explanation: The paper's Theorem 1.1 concerns the unit group of L_{F2}(1,2). The Lean theorem claims existence of a finitely presented non-sofic group. This is a different, stronger-looking claim, and the excerpt does not state finite presentability.
flags.probe_idea: State a theorem about the unit group of the Leavitt algebra (defined as a quotient of a free algebra) being not sofic under a corrected Sofic.
